title: The best books of 2026, according to the Amazon Editors
summary: Min Jin Lee’s ‘American Hagwon,’ her anticipated follow-up to ‘Pachinko,’ comes in at No. 1 from Amazon’s wide selection this year.
body_markdown:
---


## Key takeaways


- Amazon Editors selected Min Jin Lee’s


American Hagwon


as the top pick for 2026. Others on the list include


Yesteryear


by Caro Claire Burke and


Cool Machine


by Colson Whitehead.


- The 2026 list features picks across popular categories, including new Horror and Buzzworthy categories.


- Readers can explore the top 20 selections for their next favorite book or holiday gift from Amazon’s wide selection.


---


Each month, the Amazon Editors reveal our picks for the


[Best Books of the Month](https://www.amazon.com/gp/browse.html?rw_useCurrentProtocol=1&node=17143709011&ref_=amb_link_TvmpCrrERLWeDFjtdvhEsg_1) . As the end of the year approaches, we play favorites, and after much discussion and debate, we select the


[Best Books of the Year](https://www.amazon.com/best-books-2024/b?ie=UTF8&node=17276804011) .


While many of the books on this list are distinctly of the moment, others are destined to become timeless classics, including our No. 1 pick, Min Jin Lee’s


[American Hagwon](https://www.amazon.com/American-Hagwon-Min-Jin-Lee-ebook/dp/B0GCZGJHKG?th=1) —a moving exploration of ambition, education, immigrant life and the sacrifices we make for those we love.


[How Kindle helps you stay immersed in every book you read](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/books-and-authors/kindle-recaps-feature-ebook-series-refreshers)


U.S. customers can catch up on Kindle books they’re reading, recall series plots, and get instant spoiler-free answers.


Our full list of the Best Books of 2026 has something for every reader, including biographies and memoirs, literature and fiction, history, mystery, and romantasy. And new this year, we’ve added Horror and Buzzworthy categories that have been staples of the cultural conversation.


Explore our top 20 picks below.

1.


American Hagwon


by Min Jin Lee


“An extraordinary Trojan horse of a novel that will make your heart sing and make you want to talk to everybody you know about it. Utterly magnetic, American Hagwon


will change the way you think about family, sacrifice, and education. Min Jin Lee has written (another) once-in-a-lifetime read.” — Al Woodworth, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GCZGJHKG?th=1)


2.


Exit Party


by Emily St. John Mandel


“A sparkling, genre-busting gift of a novel, Emily St. John Mandel’s latest is dystopian fiction that shook me to my core. Spanning continents, timelines, and perhaps even universes, Exit Party


makes for a glorious puzzle, one with pieces that fit together seamlessly.” — Annabel Gutterman, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Exit-Party-Emily-John-Mandel-ebook/dp/B0G777JLNG/ref=sr_1_1?crid=3UFOYNPRPPOR8&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9._LU-IUut4jyDN-d41M1WpA.QZBdtjG0YZzVSxG_O_SgUJD9V52OO4PCVh-FNUqVsfQ&dib_tag=se&keywords=B0G777JLNG&nsdOptOutParam=true&qid=1791476207&sprefix=b0g777jlng%2Caps%2C193&sr=8-1)


3.


The Vanishing Family: Love, Fate, and the Quest to End Dementia


by Robert Kolker


“Robert Kolker’s enthralling medical mystery is both mesmerizing and heartbreaking—it asks big questions about chance and choice, what makes a full life, what we’re willing to run toward (or hide from), and how we care for each other. It’s a true story that will stick with you.” — Lindsay Powers, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Vanishing-Family-Love-Quest-Dementia-ebook/dp/B0GFCRKJDH/ref=sr_1_1?crid=N8JJ0UN9E4S0&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.LdtfEIMjowNRrl0WFw4etvjNnNDx8HvDKRBdwRAyZll5BS7qz5NG8T2ZbrAtRamKuvEtgmRsuXmFDYJ2UHc5YwKe6yUnxXyPl0LS6mckh7kIPBAb2AgANA2xbNN5YNOWCJozzuJTUofw3AAiVw2ZGRLQIyKH8TcCuWk4YvKPLRSgRlv1K1ePKtEW33T7sGalj1tm08RZGrSVFErb_8CFIxqbeaWJOhpqiadTe4yUN38.QxYcr4zqk73o-Ml25kJ4CK054Z-Y_oMtUkln-0JdAYo&dib_tag=se&keywords=the+vanishing+family&qid=1791562989&sprefix=the+vanishing+family%2Caps%2C199&sr=8-1)

Audible’s 'Harry Potter' audiobooks feature Hugh Laurie, Matthew Macfadyen, and more than 200 voice actors.


4.


Kin


by Tayari Jones


“This was our pick for the best book of the year so far, and our love for this novel about two motherless friends coming of age in the Jim Crow South endures. A nuanced portrait of friendship, family, and race—Jones’ sentences sing.” — Erin Kodicek, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Kin-Oprahs-Book-Club-Novel-ebook/dp/B0FPL3QMCQ/ref=sr_1_7?crid=35C14VK0H5F09&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.kk3k7yvkAJr-bv-L6WPGEw.mWvDv2cpiSuEAEkRcI9l8sTLSUNHxX4R-aSfwi_y-os&dib_tag=se&keywords=B0FPL3QMCQ&nsdOptOutParam=true&qid=1791476286&sprefix=b0fpl3qmcq%2Caps%2C146&sr=8-7&th=1)


5.


Fruit Fly


by Josh Silver


“Walking the line between hysterical and horrifying, this electric psychological thriller ruthlessly takes on cultural appropriation through a delicious cat-and-mouse game like no other. If you’re in a reading slump, Fruit Fly


is the cure.” — Abby Abell, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Fruit-Fly-Novel-Josh-Silver-ebook/dp/B0FZRXR7DR/ref=tmm_kin_swatch_0?_encoding=UTF8&dib_tag=se&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.N1zN_QnMDDe0rnXFm1cL6A.zOYhXA4YFNfaOurlzp9mKqIcDKD4KUoWhJo-HOVuvuo&qid=1791476314&sr=8-1&th=1)


6.


Land


by Maggie O’Farrell


“Never before have a 19th-century mapmaker, a scruffy, loyal dog, and a mysterious copse of trees been more enchanting. O’Farrell delivers a soaring and bewitching tale of family and how the remote Irish peninsula where they live defines and shapes them, generation after generation.” — Al Woodworth, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Land-Novel-Maggie-OFarrell-ebook/dp/B0FPKGHKRV/ref=sr_1_3?crid=2MGQ4V3DKSFJP&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.L6aclxNXtQvp-I76pbkNkQ.IeuWX1UM-Sbiizd8NYFx68rOpYvcY47rDFhREFsvAhc&dib_tag=se&keywords=B0FPKGHKRV&nsdOptOutParam=true&qid=1791476369&sprefix=b0fpkghkrv%2Caps%2C146&sr=8-3&th=1)


7.


by Patrick Radden Keefe


“Illuminating and unforgettable, Patrick Radden Keefe’s latest delivers another knockout work of narrative nonfiction, this time telling the shocking story of how a young man got caught up in the dangerous and powerful world of Russian oligarchs and landed at the bottom of the Thames.” — Al Woodworth, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/London-Falling-Mysterious-Gilded-Familys-ebook/dp/B0FGZYTRP1/ref=sr_1_1?crid=1WYUMY2MRV0Y7&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9._nne204PEorRrlKyYu-zfw.QDKUY8ULcDLJ972D7JbvmJxtxw5nsBV7ZXWGUeR6cEA&dib_tag=se&keywords=B0FGZYTRP1&nsdOptOutParam=true&qid=1791476397&sprefix=b0fgzytrp1%2Caps%2C188&sr=8-1)


8.


Big Little Truths


by Liane Moriarty


“The many fans of Big Little Lies


will love this follow-up, but you don’t need to have read that book or seen the show to enjoy Big Little Truths


. I’ve been a fan of Liane Moriarty since her early books, and this is simply one of her very best. The dialogue is so clever, and the storytelling so engrossing, you won’t be able to put this book down.” — Sarah Gelman, Editorial Director


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Big-Little-Truths-Reeses-Sequel-ebook/dp/B0GHS31MJJ/ref=sr_1_1?crid=3AF5KLJH6GOT6&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.UIx4dQnxaLWhEDCGfLwS2Q.YqzTPrGvclzUeD1LsYUDjGeB660c9S06TlEoUBztXDQ&dib_tag=se&keywords=B0GHS31MJJ&nsdOptOutParam=true&qid=1791476425&sprefix=b0ghs31mjj%2Caps%2C185&sr=8-1&th=1)

9.


This Cursed Beautiful Land: A Russian-American Story


by Evan Gershkovich


“This heart-pounding, reported memoir sucked me in from the first page; it’s a gripping account of resilience and perseverance that goes far beyond the headlines to reveal what really happened to Evan Gershkovich when he was snatched off the street and thrown into a Russian prison.” — Lindsay Powers, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/This-Cursed-Beautiful-Land-Russian-American-ebook/dp/B0GJJL1CQ1/ref=sr_1_1?crid=3CYJEGF4KCXTW&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.qCdCmYau0PahMcs6tUy7Rw.BsKbFfV-CbYW4uMHiM6Pr21WKCguWODR3tSJP-SFmxw&dib_tag=se&keywords=B0GJJL1CQ1&nsdOptOutParam=true&qid=1791476446&sprefix=b0gjjl1cq1%2Caps%2C199&sr=8-1)


10.


Cool Machine


by Colson Whitehead


“Two-time Pulitzer Prize winner Colson Whitehead delivers another searing page-turner of heists, gangsters, criminals, and families in this mesmerizing portrait of 1980s New York City.” — Al Woodworth, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Cool-Machine-Novel-Harlem-Trilogy-ebook/dp/B0FX7Z2KMJ/ref=sr_1_1?crid=1XKW7EM1GT100&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.v97qpQhYXBjmWSXSFCvfEw.iXEHVX2qMqytd5nqd5rDr2TKLVqie1MusUIKG5KVSrQ&dib_tag=se&keywords=B0FX7Z2KMJ&nsdOptOutParam=true&qid=1791476475&sprefix=b0fx7z2kmj%2Caps%2C223&sr=8-1)


11.


Whale Harbor


by Mary Beth Keane


“I’m guessing most authors can’t help but compete with themselves, and when you have novels like The Half Moon


, Fever,


and Ask Again, Yes


in your repertoire, that competition is particularly stiff. But Mary Beth Keane has risen to the occasion, yet again, with this poignant family saga.” — Erin Kodicek, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Whale-Harbor-Mary-Beth-Keane-ebook/dp/B0GP8XGGDJ/ref=sr_1_1?crid=5A1Q2YJEQOSB&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.eu0ZzZLdGTaKnsAh6TmEur6Mdq6tqU9ALeoCVBc0Bj5S1i-SuMGyqwIYg43PuEl1-GyuS7m7gt3MkklkmbE0sSaQtC85q03WD7GZhH2Q5_K3b-xTAJpO18k4qgZ6l00b31tGCenOL7svRp2VKILZnjFL-Fp7imvMrLEENSfZwAfLTKQw0sIxELRDl3Xmo-ZPPpAG3A6hMqNpMF-S-BMeVkkHDpF9gc1Xpif6c_1ZJc0.d3etFChL8hiBJCiLqdJDdN9a5cbYkgPW1P8KuV_hsls&dib_tag=se&keywords=11.+Whale+Harbor+by+Mary+Beth+Keane&qid=1793255748&sprefix=11.+whale+harbor+by+mary+beth+keane%2Caps%2C756&sr=8-1)


12.


Luna, Phoenix, Queen


by Julie Orringer


“Reminiscent of Lily King’s Writers & Lovers and Meg Wolitzer’s The Wife, Luna, Phoenix, Queen is a deeply affecting, beautifully written book about love, fidelity, faithfulness, and loss. You will wish it went on for hundreds of pages more.” — Sarah Gelman, Editorial Director


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Luna-Phoenix-Queen-Julie-Orringer-ebook/dp/B0GGJ8BD4Y/ref=sr_1_1?crid=1POIVI8QDHG3C&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.xIlJ61bLrK7KVJs_nLeCjg.NLgzCfD2nJJ96GIo8VGqxH7WyfrR79vv7Q4QGGX__GU&dib_tag=se&keywords=12.+Luna%2C+Phoenix%2C+Queen+by+Julie+Orringer&qid=1793255765&sprefix=11.+whale+harbor+by+mary+beth+keane%2Caps%2C499&sr=8-1)


13.


Public Access Afterworld


by Jane Schoenbrun


“This wonderfully weird love letter to television is the perfect antidote to our screen-obsessed world. Be warned: Once you pick this glittering, genre-bending novel up, it’ll be nearly impossible to put down.” — Annabel Gutterman, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Public-Access-Afterworld-Jane-Schoenbrun-ebook/dp/B0G4MWNCRV/ref=sr_1_5?crid=2G3JVM42R5V42&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.29ZsisIGr3Ii9nPu6_gT5Q.7vlkMtc8DOYDwBt2Z2KYHN1KVHDHSe1WEX678aoaFv4&dib_tag=se&keywords=B0G4MWNCRV&nsdOptOutParam=true&qid=1793255831&sprefix=b0g4mwncrv%2Caps%2C185&sr=8-5&th=1)


[How to buy and borrow Kindle books](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/devices/how-to-buy-kindle-books)


Everything you need to know to start reading with Kindle.


14.


Bad Words


by Rioghnach Robinson


“I have found it's more difficult to write about the books I really love, and that is the case with Bad Words. It is a spectacularly written ode to books, to being seen, and to falling in love with the person you least expect. I can't wait for everyone to read it.” — Abby Abell, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Bad-Words-Novel-Rioghnach-Robinson-ebook/dp/B0G2MYPYPM/ref=sr_1_1?crid=3M9GRGKFGBSYN&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.K08flRo8fHOu712pABkyqg.J_d-YNo950dAokFIgv4WLi9t6sxjpKUy9YZ_4xJik8A&dib_tag=se&keywords=B0G2MYPYPM&nsdOptOutParam=true&qid=1793255865&sprefix=b0g2mypypm%2Caps%2C225&sr=8-1&th=1)


15.


Strangers: A Memoir of Marriage


by Belle Burden


“Strangers is a divorce memoir, but it’s also a forensic examination of a love and a marriage gone wrong, seemingly without any warning. Burden puts words to many of our worst fears, that one day the person we love and trust the most will become an utter stranger to us.” — Sarah Gelman, Editorial Director


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Strangers-Memoir-Marriage-Belle-Burden-ebook/dp/B0F3WTJ9V2/ref=tmm_kin_swatch_0?_encoding=UTF8&dib_tag=se&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.94bxK0LtE7fA52pZ3ZNKvSvebr9mdaVhpGDZz-o6xGpdoj5C54XGyTnlqweaX5JQdmh5KFJJ8mX_AjI2_oGMD04IMtfd6GGVVqlFkvpe0y14_Xti0tEBIA2kgfliEOsYNpV4JCVb89o5ZeYktrVcB1huUfas62Q-Dj2TPVMxcNkt_7iq5287SiqgtOzfEsIpoYSEdcbmXHktWlSb2omE83HGpNzl4_xV2rWDLqseqco.tmiaok4pSFX-uwLSNhfCJZ2giEE92mp1lNDd5GFF-b4&qid=1793255885&sr=8-1)


16.


John of John


by Douglas Stuart


“Set on a remote Scottish isle where you can feel the damp in your bones, John of John tells the story of a family reunion complicated by the secrets its members are keeping from each other. Stuart dazzles in the monumental but quiet moments that make a life.” — Al Woodworth, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/John-Douglas-Stuart-ebook/dp/B0FBHMWRRQ/ref=tmm_kin_swatch_0?_encoding=UTF8&dib_tag=se&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.Io4qfKJZT07Nj8-Va8qcf2A5Q07iZwlhqvSfYF4wyJSdPQ9Xclw-kRZlji7iDbtgpEYtFvvhDWYnaCoSdGxsTk0vx4vodFWzfL9zgZ-CIh31jJgei6Y3j9ZBn7s3ZpoHe_ZVDedFfyaR8LonswPTx4a9EEEdmcp3-HDbDY1dYaeqblnkHVZrh5W_1L_TaDsIvIsO6TxT4n0hwA0LiaGhuGCPRpPtyAL9oD5H7lCSDPs.U_hWVFam62E6kNToH_N_qWIDAK3iKobyZdfSNf58lOM&qid=1793255908&sr=8-1)


17.


Yesteryear


by Caro Claire Burke


“When a tradwife influencer wakes up to discover it’s somehow the 19th century, her dizzying journey back to reality makes for a brilliant, biting novel about motherhood, fame, and faith.” — Annabel Gutterman, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Yesteryear-Novel-Caro-Claire-Burke-ebook/dp/B0FH1V3D9M/ref=tmm_kin_swatch_0?_encoding=UTF8&dib_tag=se&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.eFWDD761_5RA2amtm78NBQ.-uIQgEXFhlYS2jlSje8nomxhRpVUEbf8QpVzQ5L-mHI&qid=1793255929&sr=8-1&th=1)


18.


The Disappearers


by Marlon James


“In this decades-spanning epic feat of a novel, Marlon James traces the aftermath of a brutally violent attack on a group of gay men in 1980s Jamaica. He creates a dazzling maximalist portrait of queerness, identity, and survival that fires on all cylinders: It’s haunting, horrific, hilarious, and bursting with heart.” — Annabel Gutterman, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Disappearers-Novel-Marlon-James-ebook/dp/B0GJ755BD7/ref=tmm_kin_swatch_0?_encoding=UTF8&dib_tag=se&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.IoSgRwPsnAwtB8CfYDvHNbSr6vTooIsumA_GK40Gg1JOjNMmkQTsY5uACGGLvIRO.Hft2BVn3Qi-b6SbUTu6PrMO-3gsPzw-cB9GfqFPj14M&qid=1793255949&sr=8-1)


19.


The Nightingales


by Emil Wilson


“This emotional graphic novel finds a high school student and the dying man her dad invites into their household forming an unlikely and powerful friendship—one that will fuel the trajectory of the former’s life. It’s a story—full of heart, and thankfully plenty of humor—that readers will immediately recognize as not just good, but special.” — Erin Kodicek, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Nightingales-Emil-Wilson-ebook/dp/B0FX5R6JNT/ref=sr_1_1?crid=1N33GN4LRLN0N&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.oBlbQtQMxSdRdhi9_Fwx3g.G2KVVm9Hua3GcGicFLQ1EoOG0612zscmuFv372g1gQI&dib_tag=se&keywords=B0FX5R6JNT&nsdOptOutParam=true&qid=1793255988&sprefix=%2Caps%2C196&sr=8-1)


20.


Night Objects


by Eli Raphael


“This mesmerizing suspense novel about a teenager’s desperate search for belonging at her elite boarding school—where secrets swirl and danger looms large—lived in my head for days. Eli Raphael introduces herself as a writer you don’t want to miss.” — Annabel Gutterman, Amazon Editor


[Learn more](https://www.amazon.com/Night-Objects-Novel-Eli-Raphael-ebook/dp/B0FVWY7LVC/ref=sr_1_1?crid=U0NJWTS1Y8M7&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.Zo63NNS_gFauyqzkYvKb5A.R3L8Ce3Zb49hZ6yCAi7EAFvfXclbtZjuu0oUcCyroi8&dib_tag=se&keywords=20.%2BNight%2BObjects%2Bby%2BEli%2BRaphael&qid=1793256008&sprefix=20.%2Bnight%2Bobjects%2Bby%2Beli%2Braphael%2Caps%2C257&sr=8-1&th=1)
